claim.quote: Evidence for oscillation of atmospheric neutrinos

date.note: Announced June 1998 (Neutrino '98 conference, per the SK history page); published as PRL 81, 1562 (1998).
date.quote: Discovery of atmospheric neutrino oscillations announced.

key_value_text.quote: a zenith angle dependent deficit of muon neutrinos which is inconsistent with expectations based on calculations of the atmospheric neutrino flux
key_value_text.value: Zenith-angle-dependent deficit of muon neutrinos inconsistent with expectations for no oscillation; data consistent with two-flavour nu_mu <-> nu_tau oscillation.

name: Super-Kamiokande evidence for atmospheric neutrino oscillation

summary.plain: In 1998, Super-Kamiokande found that neutrinos made in the atmosphere seemed to 'disappear' depending on how far they had travelled through the Earth - the first strong evidence that neutrinos change type, and therefore have mass.
summary.technical: 33.0 kiloton-year exposure; observed a zenith-angle-dependent muon-neutrino deficit inconsistent with the no-oscillation expectation, consistent with two-flavour nu_mu <-> nu_tau oscillation. The collaboration's own title states 'evidence', not 'discovery' or 'observation'.

title: Evidence for oscillation of atmospheric neutrinos
why_it_matters: The result that first convinced the field neutrinos oscillate (and hence have mass), contradicting the Standard Model's massless-neutrino assumption; foundational to the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physics (shared with SNO).
